theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas is the highest-ranked and most durable eligible theme with strong breadth, satisfying the trend-gate leg which is the one validated risk-control edge. The high crowding flag (z=1.04) is a size-down caution, not a fade, and the mixed Hurst tag plus modest r10 suggests momentum is real but not accelerating.
evidence: absolute_trend_gate validated for drawdown avoidance on this market (gate_helps true)
theses.dissent: Oil & Gas is crowded and energy leadership often peaks late-cycle when macro growth narrative is shifting; the theme's own momentum is not a return forecast and a commodity pullback would hit hardest here.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO lags the S&P/TSX composite by 3% over any 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the confirmed challenger (score 1.11, rank 2), eligible, uncrowded (z=0.2), and still trend-healthy by the absolute-trend gate. The low breadth (0.267) means leadership is narrow but the rotation margin to the leader (0.502) is wide, suggesting this is a genuine second theme rather than a crowded co-attention spike.
evidence: rotation challenger id ca_gold with margin 0.502
theses.dissent: Low breadth means a few large-cap miners are carrying the theme; if those names stall the whole theme stalls, and the mean-revert flag on adjacent metals mining suggests mean-reversion risk is present.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms XEG.TO by 4% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Uranium & Nuclear
theses.thesis: Uranium & Nuclear is ineligible (rank 16, score -1.555, durability 0.14) and fails the absolute-trend gate, which is the one validated risk-control leg. This is a non-trend theme that should be avoided under trend discipline.
evidence: absolute-trend gate validated for drawdown avoidance (gate_helps true)
theses.dissent: Uranium can produce sudden speculative bursts on supply headlines; the gate is about avoiding drawdowns and may miss a genuine breakout if urgency appears.
